title: The carried low batch
desiredOutcome: Every low review finding carried to BUG-29-dau is fixed in the code, or answered with the evidence that nothing is left to change, and the bug closes

findings.issue: sr39 failed on the windows resample leg of run 40781798399 (c35ffffb): exit 3 in 7.1 s but the basis did not say timed out. The case builds a first run sleeping 3 s under a 7 s deadline, so whether the deadline lands in the second run, in the first, or not at all depends on how fast the runner starts interpreters; on a loaded windows runner the first run can eat the budget.
findings.resolution: Make sr39 independent of runner speed: drive the cut-off with a witness rather than a sleep sized against the deadline (as tt3c in tools/sweep-selftests.py does), so the second run is reached and cut off on any runner; keep the assertion that one deadline covers both runs.

findings.file: tests/_harness.py:2254-2295 (sr3d, sr19c) and the task's tests.gate
findings.issue: The recorded gate command selects tools/sweep-selftests.py, tools/_suite.py, tools/gate-parity.py, tests/test_import_evidence.py and tests/test_run_test_gate.py, but not tests/_harness.py, which holds the largest part of the diff: the reach, id-reading and print changes and their cases sr3d and sr19c (and sr18, the case the P142-R21 finding is about). So the gate record says nothing about P144-R7/R8/R9, P142-R26 or P142-R21. I ran tests/_harness.py --selftest once in the task tree: exit 0, 98/98 cases passed, sr3d and sr19c PASS, so nothing is wrong today. The executor discloses this but leaves it open. The P142-R21 finding is therefore only half answered: sr18's red-first proof is claimed, the gate-record half is not made.
findings.resolution: Add `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/_harness.py` (or the file) to this task's tests.gate; the manifest edit is outside the declared files, so the orchestrator does it.

findings.issue: P132-R6 is not made. The executor's reason holds in the tree: the three sites it names exist at HEAD (tests/test__doctor_trail.py:495 shutil.rmtree(journal_dir(wiped)), tests/test_audit_task.py:14728 shutil.rmtree(wt), tests/test_drive_phase.py:10696 shutil.rmtree(first + '.redo-5')). It is reported rather than fixed, which the task allows. But the phase's desired outcome ('fixed, or answered with the evidence that nothing is left to change, and the bug closes') is not met for this id: the coverage loss (a plain rmtree over a git-written directory is not convicted) is still in the code.
findings.resolution: Carry P132-R6 to a follow-up task whose scope holds tests/test__doctor_trail.py, tests/test_audit_task.py and tests/test_drive_phase.py (switch the three sites to _harness.remove_tree), then drop the early-continue and turn s21 into the init-only allow case. Do not close the bug over it.

findings.issue: The cw10b label writes a cardinality into prose ('exactly the two whose writers format the name inline') beside a check that pins those rows by prefix. A third inline-formatted row would make the sentence false while the check says what it checks. The task says no number written into prose; a word under ten is legal to the lint, so this is author-enforced, not a lint failure.
findings.resolution: Drop 'the two' from the label and name the pinned rows (journal pre-image, TDD reminder) only, as the comment above it already does.

findings.issue: P131-R7 is answered in part. The finding named the leaked handles in x2 and in x4/rl16. x2 and x4 now read through a with block. rl16 still reads `texts = {n: io.open(os.path.join(folder, n), encoding="utf-8").read() ...}`, so the handle is still left to the GC. The outcome says rl16 is 'left as it is' because release.py is not a declared file, which is the declared-files rule at work, but the finding stays half open.
findings.resolution: Carry the rl16 half forward (or add tools/release.py to a task's files) and replace the comprehension's io.open().read() with a with-block read, as x4 now does.

findings.issue: P145-R1 is answered in part. The finding offered 'fail loudly or name the spelling exercised', and the second was done: pw5's text now prints `exercised: ... NOT exercised`. Two things remain. The conjunct `respelled is None and os.name == "nt"` still lets pw5 pass on a Windows runner that cannot make the link. And the finding's second request, confirming on a windows-latest run that pw5, pw6 and pw13 pass with the symlink branch taken, is not done. The outcome defers it to the next Windows CI log, which cannot be read here.
findings.resolution: Leave the finding open on that one confirmation: after the next windows-latest log, check that the pw5 line reads 'a second spelling, through a link'. If it reads 'NOT exercised', make the case fail on nt.

findings.issue: The sentence 'A mutation that turns nothing red is printed as `inert`' is now a subset of the behaviour. inert also covers a mutation whose only reds were already red unmutated or green when swept again, and the CI tail now prints WINDOW TRUNCATED. The executor reported this and left it, since the file is outside the task. The doc and the tool now disagree, but only by understatement, and no other document pins the old wording.
findings.resolution: In a follow-up that owns CONTRIBUTING.md, reword to 'a mutation that changes no suite's verdict' and add the truncation line.
